title: The bowtie monster and its yell
summary: The bowtie monster announces itself with a yell heard across the level: the game gives it sprung head and eyes, a vertical turn of its own, stomp particles and a spark when it leaves.
body: The bowtie monster is built to be heard as much as seen. Its whole attack begins with a yell, and the yell is modelled in parts rather than as one shout.

It has a start and an end to that yell, with a loop for the time in between, and each of those has a version for the player and a version for the rest of the crew. That pair is why the same yell can sound close to one person and distant to another.
The yell has particles of its own: a big one and a small one. Keeping both means the effect can be scaled rather than drawn the same way every time.

It stomps as it moves, and each foot has a party of its own. There is a particle for the left foot and one for the right, which is how a heavy monster can be tracked by its footprints rather than only by its silhouette.
Its head and both eyes are sprung with targets, and the body turns on a horizontal spring with a vertical turn of its own. That combination is what lets it lean towards you rather than rotating flat.
It carries particle eyes along with the usual impact and directional bits, so hitting it and being looked at are both visible effects rather than only sounds.
It sparks when it leaves. There is a particle for the despawn spark and a sound for it, which is how a monster can make an exit that reads as a departure rather than a pop.

Everything else is the standard set: footsteps in two sizes, short and long movement, a jump and a landing, a notice sound, a despawn sound, its own material and a collider it can leave behind as it moves.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the colour texture of the bowtie monster.
What this entry does not tell you: how loud the yell is, how far it carries, or how much damage the monster does. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Its head and both eyes are sprung with targets, and the body turns on a horizontal spring.
facts.evidence: identifiers: headSpring, headTransform, HeadTargetTransform, eyeRightSpring, eyeRightTransform, eyeRightTargetTransform, eyeLeftSpring, eyeLeftTransform, eyeLeftTargetTransform, horizontalRotationSpring

facts.claim: It has a vertical rotation transform and a vertical rotation spring of its own.
Its yell has a start, an end and a loop, each with a player and a level version.
facts.evidence: identifiers: yellStartSound, yellStartSoundGlobal, yellEndSound, yellEndSoundGlobal, YellLoopSound, GroanLoopSound

facts.claim: The yell has a big particle and a small one.
It stomps with a separate particle for each foot.
It has particle eyes, impact and directional bits, and a despawn spark with a sound.
facts.evidence: identifiers: particleEyes, particleImpact, particleDirectionalBits, particleDespawnSpark, despawnSparkSound

facts.claim: It has footsteps in two sizes, short and long movement, jump and landing, notice and despawn sounds.
facts.evidence: identifiers: footstepSound, footstepSmallSound, moveShortSound, moveLongSound, jumpSound, landSound, noticeSound, despawnSound

facts.claim: It has its own material and a hurt collider it can leave behind.
